title: Content Moderation API
summary: Integrate content classification as a versioned policy service with explicit thresholds, contextual handling, latency budgets, and review paths.
overview: A content moderation API classifies submitted material into policy-relevant categories or returns associated scores. The application decides what those classifications mean for its audience and workflow. Provider labels and confidence scores are not universal legal judgments, and thresholds should be validated against representative content.

Moderation can apply to user inputs, retrieved material, generated outputs, and uploaded media. Each surface has a different purpose: rejecting a user action, quarantining evidence, or controlling publication. Keep moderation separate from malware scanning, authorization, and factual verification, which address different failure modes.

production.poc: A prototype can score a reviewed sample and inspect false positives before enabling automatic blocking. Include legitimate discussion of sensitive topics.
production.production: Production versions the moderation policy, maps provider categories to application outcomes, and defines timeouts and outage behavior. Minimize the personal data sent to the classification service.
production.scale: At scale, asynchronous review, multilingual evaluation, and drift monitoring become necessary. Measure disagreement and appeals rather than assuming the provider's default thresholds fit every tenant or product.

components.name: Content adapter
components.role: Normalizes supported text and media while preserving the context needed for classification.

components.name: Moderation service
components.role: Produces category signals under a known model or API configuration.

components.name: Policy mapper
components.role: Converts signals into allow, block, quarantine, or review outcomes for the application.

components.name: Review workflow
components.role: Handles ambiguous cases, appeals, and high-impact decisions with accountable human judgment.

components.name: Moderation telemetry
components.role: Tracks latency, errors, decision rates, and reviewed false positives without excessive content retention.

flow.title: Identify surface
flow.description: Determine whether the content is input, evidence, output, or an uploaded asset.

flow.title: Prepare payload
flow.description: Apply size limits, data minimization, and format handling appropriate to the service.

flow.title: Request classification
flow.description: Call the API with a deadline and record its version and operational status.

flow.title: Apply policy
flow.description: Map category signals and context to explicit application decisions.

flow.title: Handle uncertainty
flow.description: Route borderline or unsupported content to review or a defined constrained path.

flow.title: Evaluate decisions
flow.description: Compare sampled outcomes with reviewed labels and update thresholds through controlled changes.

useCase.title: Reviewing seller-generated product descriptions
useCase.situation: A marketplace lets sellers use an assistant to draft descriptions and upload product imagery.
useCase.problem: Generated or uploaded content can violate marketplace rules, while crude filtering rejects legitimate safety equipment and educational products.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must screen publication against marketplace policy and give sellers an understandable review path.
useCase.architecture: Input and output adapters call a moderation service, then a policy mapper combines category signals with product context.
runtime: A seller submits a draft; the service scores relevant categories and the mapper decides whether to publish, request revision, or queue review.
A reviewer resolves ambiguous cases and records labels that support later threshold evaluation.
useCase.failure: If the moderation API times out, unpublished high-risk content remains pending under the defined policy instead of silently bypassing screening.
useCase.impact: Track reviewed violation rate, false rejections, appeal outcomes, moderation latency, and pending-review age by content type and language.

tradeoffs.benefit: Specialized classification can be integrated quickly.
tradeoffs.cost: Latency, data handling, and provider changes become dependencies.

tradeoffs.benefit: Clear violations can be handled at volume.
tradeoffs.cost: False positives can unfairly interrupt legitimate users.
Review capacity and response time limit throughput.

failures.detection: Decision-rate drift and reviewed samples reveal a shift.
failures.recovery: Recalibrate the mapping and version the policy change.

failures.detection: Adapter coverage checks identify an unprocessed format.
failures.recovery: Reject, transform safely, or route the asset to review.

mistakes.mistake: Using provider scores as universal thresholds
Applying identical policy to evidence and publication
mistakes.fix: Define separate handling for each surface.

mistakes.mistake: Failing open accidentally during API errors
mistakes.fix: Specify and test outage behavior explicitly.

whenToUse: User or generated content needs policy-based screening.
Clear application outcomes can be mapped from category signals.
Ambiguous cases have a review or appeal path.
whenNotToUse: The requirement is malware detection or authorization alone.
No representative content exists for calibration.
The service's data handling conflicts with approved processing rules.
checklist: Define policies for each content surface.
Set request deadlines and outage behavior.
Cover supported languages and media formats.
